Here is the AI problem nobody is talking about enough: the agents are ready, but the data behind them is not.

A new report from Box found that AI agents have moved into mainstream enterprise use — but the content infrastructure supporting them has failed to keep pace. Unstructured documents, siloed knowledge bases, and fragmented data stores are creating a bottleneck that no model upgrade can fix.

The scale of what is happening makes this urgent. Google reported at I/O 2026 that it is processing 3.2 quadrillion tokens per month — a fiftyfold increase in one year. The Gemini app now has over 900 million monthly active users. Google also launched Gemini Spark, a persistent AI agent that runs continuously in the background.

Agent deployment is accelerating. But when those agents cannot reliably access and interpret your organization's content, you get hallucinations, incomplete workflows, and diminished trust in AI outputs. The model is not the weak link. The content layer is.

For executive teams, the implication is practical: the highest-return AI investment right now may not be another model subscription. It may be restructuring how your organization's knowledge is stored, tagged, and made accessible to AI systems.
